title: Close an AtlasOps cross-tenant access path

bridge.applicationConcept: Authentication, organization roles, object authorization, protected routes, and signed storage access
bridge.analogyLimit: A signed-in session proves identity, not permission to every object or route in the application.

buildBrief: Add AtlasOps operator, lead, and stakeholder journeys with organization ownership, protected routes, search, filtering, and role-appropriate controls.
incidentBrief: A server route checks only that the caller is signed in before issuing access to another organization’s record. Exploit it with synthetic accounts, fix the resource boundary, and test enumeration resistance.

scenario.symptoms: An authenticated operator can request a predictable record identifier owned by a different organization.

acceptanceTests: Role journeys expose only approved actions and records
Cross-tenant direct-object requests fail at the server and database boundaries
Authorization tests cover owned, other-tenant, missing, expired, and changed-role cases
evidence: Exploit reproduction and passing regression suite
predictionQuestions: Which boundary currently proves only identity rather than ownership?
What response avoids revealing whether the other tenant’s record exists?
defenseQuestions: Trace a protected record request through route, database, and response.
Explain authentication versus authorization using the exploit.
Remove one UI control and explain why that alone is not a security fix.
hints: Test the URL or server function directly as both synthetic users.
Authorize the requested resource, action, and organization together.
Keep database policy coverage even after adding a server ownership check.
